title: 讲座：文化的分类（新题型优化版所供原文）

sentences.en: Good morning, everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家早上好。

sentences.en: Today we’ll look at culture or rather classifications of cultures.
sentences.zh: 今天我们来谈文化，更准确地说，是文化的分类。

sentences.en: Usually when we deal with different people, we deal with them as if we were all members of the same culture.
sentences.zh: 通常，与不同的人打交道时，我们会把对方当作与自己属于同一种文化的人。

sentences.en: However, it’s possible that people from different cultures have different assumptions about the world, regarding such important and basic ideas as time, personal space.
sentences.zh: 然而，来自不同文化的人，对于世界可能有不同的基本认识，其中就涉及时间、私人空间等重要而基础的观念。

sentences.en: And this is the view of Edward Hall.
sentences.zh: 这就是爱德华·霍尔的观点。

sentences.en: And Edward Hall is an anthropologist who spent a large part of his life studying American Indians, their culture, their language, but he was different from a lot of other anthropologists who just study one culture.
sentences.zh: 爱德华·霍尔是一位人类学家，他一生中的很大一部分时间都在研究美洲印第安人及其文化和语言，但他与许多只研究单一文化的人类学家不同。

sentences.en: He was interested in the relations between cultures, how cultures interact.
sentences.zh: 他关注的是不同文化之间的关系，以及文化如何相互作用。

sentences.en: What Hall believes is that cultures can be classified by placing them on a continuum, ranging from what he called high-context to low-context.
sentences.zh: 霍尔认为，可以把各种文化放到一条连续谱上加以分类，其范围从他所说的高语境文化一直延伸到低语境文化。

sentences.en: OK, what is a high-context culture?
sentences.zh: 好，那么什么是高语境文化呢？

w.m: phr.高语境文化；强语境文化

sentences.en: A high-context culture is a culture in which the context of the message or the action or an event carries a large part of its meaning and significance.
sentences.zh: 在高语境文化中，信息、行为或事件的很大一部分含义与意义，都由其所处的语境来承载。

sentences.en: What this means is that in a high-context culture more attention is paid to what has been in and around the message than to the message itself.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，在高语境文化中，人们更关注信息的相关背景和周围情境，而不是信息本身。

sentences.en: Now let me give you examples.
sentences.zh: 现在让我举些例子。

sentences.en: First in terms of personal space, generally speaking, in a high-context culture, because there’s greater dependency on group thinking, people lean towards heavier sensory involvement or closeness to people.
sentences.zh: 首先来看私人空间。一般来说，在高语境文化中，由于人们更依赖群体思维，他们倾向于更多的感官接触，或与他人保持更近的距离。

sentences.en: And they have less respect for privacy, for personal space.
sentences.zh: 他们对隐私、对私人空间的重视程度也较低。

sentences.en: If you go into that culture, people might stand closer when they’re talking to you.
sentences.zh: 如果你进入那样的文化环境，别人与你交谈时可能会站得更近。

sentences.en: They might touch more and if they’re jostled in a crowd, they won’t feel violated.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会有更多身体接触；即使在人群中被挤碰，也不会觉得受到了侵犯。

sentences.en: And also people from a high-context culture pay attention to body language.
sentences.zh: 此外，来自高语境文化的人会关注身体语言。

sentences.en: Because remember what I said, the definition of a high-context culture is that more attention is paid to the context of the message than to the message itself, and part of the context is body language.
sentences.zh: 因为，请记住我刚才说过的定义：高语境文化更关注信息的语境，而不是信息本身；身体语言也是语境的一部分。

sentences.en: Second, in terms of time, people in high-context cultures are considered to have what is called a polychronic attitude toward time.
sentences.zh: 其次，就时间而言，高语境文化中的人被认为持有所谓的多时制时间观。

w.m: adj.多时制的；允许多件事按各自节奏进行的

sentences.en: Here “poly” means multiple and “chronic” means time.
sentences.zh: 这里，“poly”表示“多个”，“chronic”表示“时间”。

sentences.en: What this means is that they believe people, things, events have their own time and there can’t be a standard system of time for everything.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，他们认为人、事物和事件各有各的时间节奏，不可能用一套标准的时间体系来统一规定一切。

sentences.en: What this leads them to believe is that you can’t emphasize punctuality.
sentences.zh: 由此，他们认为不应过分强调准时。

sentences.en: Things happen when they are supposed to happen.
sentences.zh: 事情会在它应当发生的时候发生。

sentences.en: So there’s a different attitude toward time.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是一种不同的时间观。

sentences.en: There is no set standard of time.
sentences.zh: 时间没有固定的标准。

sentences.en: You can’t control time.
sentences.zh: 你无法控制时间。

sentences.en: Everything has its own sense of time.
sentences.zh: 万事万物都有自身的时间节奏。

sentences.en: So it’s a culture that pays little attention to time, to clock time.
sentences.zh: 所以，这种文化不太重视时间，不太重视钟表所显示的时间。

w.m: phr.钟表时间；按时钟计量的时间

sentences.en: Now, let’s move on to low-context culture.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们接着来看低语境文化。

sentences.en: A low-context culture is just the opposite.
sentences.zh: 低语境文化恰恰相反。

sentences.en: A low-context culture is one in which the message, the event or the action is a separate entity, having meaning onto itself, regardless of the surroundings or the context.
sentences.zh: 在低语境文化中，信息、事件或行为是独立的实体，自身就具有意义，不依赖周围的情境或语境。

sentences.en: That the message, the event, the action has meaning in itself.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，信息、事件和行为本身就有意义。

sentences.en: So what this means in a low-context culture is that people pay more attention to the event itself rather than to the context which surrounds the event or the message.
sentences.zh: 因此，在低语境文化中，人们更关注事件本身，而不是事件或信息所处的背景。

sentences.en: For example, in terms of personal space again.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们再以私人空间为例。

sentences.en: There’s more emphasis on individuality, so the concept of privacy is very very important, or as before as I said, in a high-context culture they might not even be concerned with privacy or personal space.
sentences.zh: 这里更强调个体性，所以隐私的观念非常、非常重要；而正如我前面所说，在高语境文化中，人们可能甚至不太在意隐私或私人空间。

sentences.en: But in a low-context culture, there’s a feeling that we each have our own personal space.
sentences.zh: 但在低语境文化中，人们认为，每个人都有属于自己的私人空间。

sentences.en: If you get too close, if you don’t knock on doors before entering, that’s an invasion of privacy; people feel violated.
sentences.zh: 如果你靠得太近，或者进门之前不敲门，那就是侵犯隐私，人们会感到受到了侵犯。

sentences.en: There’s a respect and a desire for privacy, and you also see that people might pay less attention to body language because as I said the message is, the message is everything.
sentences.zh: 人们尊重并且渴望拥有隐私；你也会发现，他们可能不太关注身体语言，因为正如我所说，信息才是……信息才是一切。

sentences.en: They are not going to worry about all the details around it.
sentences.zh: 他们不会在意围绕信息的所有细节。

sentences.en: What you say is the important thing or what you do is the important thing.
sentences.zh: 重要的是你说了什么，或者你做了什么。

sentences.en: Another example of a low-context culture is people’s attitude towards time.
sentences.zh: 低语境文化的另一个例子，是人们对时间的态度。

sentences.en: In terms of time, I said before there was a polychronic sense of time in a high-context culture.
sentences.zh: 说到时间，我前面提过，高语境文化具有多时制的时间观。

sentences.en: What do you think there would be in a low-context culture?
sentences.zh: 你们认为，低语境文化会有怎样的时间观呢？

w.m: phr.低语境文化；弱语境文化

sentences.en: Monochronic! Right!
sentences.zh: 单时制！没错！

w.m: adj.单时制的；遵循统一时间表的

sentences.en: A monochronic sense of time and by that we mean that there is one time.
sentences.zh: 这是一种单时制的时间观，也就是说，只有一套统一的时间。

sentences.en: And that concept means that people in a low-context culture believe that there’s one standard of time and that should be for everything.
sentences.zh: 这种观念意味着，低语境文化中的人认为，存在一套统一的时间标准，而且万事都应遵守它。

sentences.en: And so I’m not willing to hear “Oh, the traffic was heavy. That’s why I am late.” or “Oh, I slept late.”
sentences.zh: 所以，我不愿听到“噢，交通太拥堵，所以我迟到了”，或者“噢，我睡过头了”这样的解释。

sentences.en: People in a low-context culture would be much more upset with lateness because they feel that everyone should follow the same time; there shouldn’t be all this flexibility with time and they expect punctuality.
sentences.zh: 低语境文化中的人会更难以接受迟到，因为他们认为，每个人都应遵守同一套时间，不应当对时间有这么大的弹性，而且他们要求准时。

sentences.en: And they look at time as almost a commodity that they use expressions like “use time”, “to waste time”, “to spend time” or “time is money”.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎把时间看作一种商品，因此会使用“利用时间”“浪费时间”“花费时间”，或者“时间就是金钱”这样的表达。

sentences.en: All of these expressions reinforce the concept that time is actually something you can hold onto.
sentences.zh: 所有这些表达，都强化了这样一种观念：时间实际上是可以把握在手中的东西。

sentences.en: So what this is all about is that Hall stresses that people need to be aware of these different assumptions or concepts about reality.
sentences.zh: 所以，归根结底，霍尔强调的是，人们需要意识到，不同文化对现实有着这些不同的预设或观念。

sentences.en: And he thinks that this has all kinds of relevance no matter what you’re doing, if you’re in business, negotiations, interpersonal relations, if you’re dealing with people from different cultures in any way, it’s going to affect every part of your life.
sentences.zh: 他认为，无论你从事什么，这些差异都与你密切相关：无论是商业活动、谈判，还是人际交往，只要你以任何方式与来自不同文化的人打交道，它就会影响你生活的各个方面。

sentences.en: In any multicultural situation, these assumptions need to be taken into account for successful interactions.
sentences.zh: 在任何多元文化的情境中，要实现成功的互动，都需要把这些预设考虑在内。

sentences.en: OK. Today, we’ve taken a brief look at Edward Hall’s view of culture, mainly his classification of high or low context culture with some examples.
sentences.zh: 好，今天我们简要了解了爱德华·霍尔的文化观，主要是他对高、低语境文化的分类，并看了一些例子。

sentences.en: Next week, we’ll look at some more examples of cultures on the continuum between high-context and low-context cultures.
sentences.zh: 下周，我们会进一步了解处于高语境与低语境文化连续谱上的其他文化实例。
